notes: A player command in a room with a mobile whose script has MS_ONCMD runs its oncmd; a TRUE return ends the command (Hisczdrezzez, 144/hisc.lua, blocks south).

oncmd's argument is the resolved command name plus the raw rest of the line, so s, sou and 'south please' all reach no_move() as south. The port passed the typed word, and s walked past the block. Where special() runs in the pipeline is DP-1336.
act() with the script's me, obj and vict tables resolved through their struct handles; TO_NOTVICT and TO_VICT audiences.
say() is do_say as me; the verb follows the line's last character (states/asks/exclaims/says).
After the object moves and the give lines are shown, a mobile with MS_ONGIVE runs ongive with the giver as ch and the object as obj.
ch, me, obj and room tables carry C's fields; me.objs lists the mobile's inventory in carrying order, so the just-given object is first (obj_to_char prepends) and count_piece sees the duplicate.
tell(name, text) is do_tell(me, ' name text'): the giver sees '$n tells you'.

action(me, 'give <alias> <name>') runs command_interpreter as the mobile; return_obj gives the object back. With a duplicate runestone the healer also falls through to 'What do I need this rubbish for?' and hands back the stone it had kept: C's script, reproduced.

strfind, strsub and gsub are Lua 5.1's string.find/sub/gsub. The port's wrappers used the C stack API shape (GetGlobal/GetField do not push in gopher-lua), so every call invoked its first argument: no_move and return_obj never worked. tonumber had the same wrapper over the builtin.
format was not defined at all; gopher-lua's string.format also prints %u as Go's %!u(int64=2000). Lua 4 prints %u/%o/%x/%X from (unsigned int).
assemble_one extracts the tooth and oloads 11021 to the giver.
save_char(ch) writes ch.gold back (2500 - 2000 = 500 in score).
On number(0,15) == 0, after mp_sound, a mobile with MS_SOUND runs sound when a non-mobile is in the room. The port never ran sound scripts.
The sound script's number() draws land between the wander and aggression draws, byte-identical over 8000 pulses with weather interleaved (R3).
action(me, 'sigh') runs the social as the mobile.

table_to_char reads stack slot 1 and pops nothing, so both write-back calls apply the ch table: ch is written twice, me never. A script's change to me is lost even when me is ch (never_die.lua would do nothing; it is attached to no mobile). C's clamps: align +-1000, gold/level/pos/timer/bank/exp/jail/tattoo >= 0, hp/mana/move unclamped.
No write-back unless ch->in_room > 0 (real room number, not vnum).
retval = (int)lua_tonumber(top): any nonzero integer part handles the event; 0.5, nil and FALSE do not; '1' coerces.

A binding that reaches another script (action give -> ongive, raw_kill -> death) runs it nested on the same state, as C does; the outer script continues with the globals the inner run set. The port deadlocked on its engine mutex.
ch, me, room, obj and argument are set only when run_script has them and are never cleared.
Every line a mobile runs draws number(0,3) for AFF_HIDE first, known command or not (R3).
In a nested run_script, stack slot 1 is the calling binding's first argument, not the ch table, so C's write-back applies that table instead. No live script reaches this; the port writes ch back.
special() runs after command resolution and the position check, in C's room/equipment/inventory/mobile/object order; the port runs specials and oncmd before resolution (DP-1336).
A mobile's action() line runs say, tell, emote, give and socials; other commands are logged and ignored rather than guessed at. No live script uses another.
C keeps every function a script file defines in the shared state; the port removes script-defined globals after each run.
A script's me.timer write sets GET_MOB_WAIT; the port stores it but combat does not yet honour it. No live script writes timer.
table_to_room dereferences the NULL struct room_to_table never sets: undefined behaviour, not game behaviour (R1a). The port logs and changes nothing.
hisc's fight() dofiles scripts/mob/cleric.lua, which C's lib/scripts does not have; the call fails in C and in the port.
